page.layout: One page of text, single column. Running head at top with page number at top right. Main text below. Headings "DE VERBO." and "Quid est Verbum?" centred below a horizontal rule. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: persona sæpè sunt reciproca, ut דבר deba-ró, verbum suum.

p.i: הוא hu, is qui, ISTI, ISTÆ:
מי mi, quis, quæ, de homine interrogat:
מה mah, quid? de quacunq; re alia interrogant:
אשר ascher, relativum, qui, quæ, quod.

Quando Dativus pronominis primitivi post אשר ascher, ponitur, fit inde pronomè possessivum, quod absolutè sine substantivo usurpatur: ut, אשר לי ascher li, meus, mea, meum: אשר לנו ascher lanú, noster, nostra, nostrum: אשר לך ascher lechá, tuus, a, tuum, &c.

main_text.head: DE VERBO.
Quid est Verbum?
main_text.p: VErbum est vox numeri cum forma, persona, tempore & conjugatione.

page.notes: Hebrew and Greek-style words are transcribed with the characters as printed where legible; several Hebrew vowel points are approximate. The Hebrew word at the start of the first line is printed as דבר. The ampersand "&" stands for the printed "&" with a conjunction sign form in places. Some Hebrew forms in the paradigm are partly illegible due to scan quality and may contain small errors in pointing. The line "qui, isti, istæ" is printed in italic with capitals "ISTI, ISTÆ" as shown in the scan; the first word of that line is "qui," as printed.
